They show a first handful and add more as you scroll down. This page works the same way: eight products to start, eight more each time you near the bottom, five times, and then “No more items.” With Infinite scroll on: 40 rows collected as the feed loaded, and the crawl stopped on its own at the end. Why it is tricky When the page opens, only the first eight exist, and nothing on the page says how many more are coming. A tool that reads the page once gets eight rows and looks finished. Magic Scraper scrolls, waits for the new products, adds them, and stops on its own when scrolling brings nothing new. How to do it Open Magic Scraper on this page, go to the Crawl tab, tick Infinite scroll and press Start crawling. Watch the count climb; it stops by itself at the end. What you should get 40 rows with no repeats, each with name, maker, a price like $192.00, the rating as a number, the stock line and the SKU. Eight rows means the scrolling never started; 16 or 24 means it stopped before the feed caught up. Try it yourself: get Magic Scraper free and open it on this page.
